report.label: AI-summarized (Claude) from the figures on this page; every number checked against the data
report.text:
**What happened this year.** Your 4 compactors in this region were emptied 163 times and produced about 205.1 tonnes of waste. In 81 of those visits (49.7 %) the container was less than 60 % full. 31 visits look early enough that a person should review the schedule behind them.

**What it cost.** Today you pay per visit: about €28,218 over the last 12 months, or €137.6 per tonne.

**Is your operator keeping the contract?** 68.3 % of visits happened within 2 hours of the scheduled time, and 1 visit(s) were missed. The weighbridge ticket was shared within 7 days for 93.9 % of visits. 24 invoice lines differ from your contract terms, about €1,111 above what the contract says in total. These are prompts to ask, not accusations: access problems, reschedules or a calculator gap can explain a difference.

**What could change.** If your containers were emptied when they are actually full, the same waste would need between 132 and 116 visits instead of 163: at least the 31 flagged visits fewer, and up to 47 fewer (28.8 %) if every lift were triggered by weight. In a per-kg tender where every operator can see the same weight data, our simulation puts the price at about €19,228, or €93.8 per tonne: €8,990 (31.9 %) less than today.

**What we suggest you decide.** Invite operators to bid on per-kg terms when your contract comes up, with lifts triggered by weight. Your current operator can bid too. Billing stays on the operator's certified weighbridge, exactly as today.

**What this is not.** These figures are a simulation on synthetic data with assumptions you can see on this page. They are not a guaranteed saving. Nothing is sent to any operator unless you approve it.

premature.rule: Flag a lift when the device weight shows a load under 40 % of the device's typical full payload (fill under 40 % where no weight exists) and no public reason explains it: scheduled lifts above the minimum frequency, and fill-triggered orders whose weight stays low. Maximum-interval, pre-closure, decommission, ad-hoc and customer-requested lifts are not flagged.

definitions.discrepant_line_share: Share of invoice lines whose amount differs from the contract-expected amount by more than one cent. A difference is not an error by itself: tariff versions, mass basis and calculator gaps also cause differences.
definitions.jobs: Jobs the operator was asked to do in the month: completed, partial, missed by operator, wasted trip.
definitions.missed_visit_share: Share of jobs recorded as missed by the operator. A site closure or access problem can be recorded the same way.
definitions.on_time_share: Share of completed lifts done within 2 h of the scheduled time. Late lifts can have causes outside the operator (blocked access, weather, customer reschedules).
definitions.ticket_lag_days_median: Median days from weighing to sharing, over shared tickets. Tickets shared after the data extraction are not visible, so the lag is a lower bound.
definitions.ticket_share: Share of completed lifts whose weighbridge ticket was shared with the customer within 7 days. Depends on the data-sharing agreement, not only on the operator.
definitions.tonnes_per_lift: Device-estimated tonnes per completed lift that has a device weight (estimate, not a weighbridge figure). Low values can come from early lifts the customer ordered.

economics_check.reading: Today's price = invoiced amount, which matches the contract-expected amount to the cent for most collections; the rest are billing discrepancies. Collection cost per lift is close to constant per device (median CV), so scaling trip costs with the number of lifts is a fair approximation.

validation.method: Kit scorer europress_data.evaluate (score_b, score_b2), validation split. OpenWeight rule on the as-of view at the validation end; kit B2 rules and B4 gradient boosting as run by the kit (B4 trained on train-period labels).

scorecard_b2.note: overall = the kit's 0-100 score over all 9 Task B2 metrics; metrics we do not produce (over/undercharge %, weight bias, order-to-lift) score 0 there. overall_covered_metrics = mean over the 5 metrics we produce.

trips_check.reading: The labels count only lifts the dataset calls unjustified today. The trips model also merges lifts that are justified under today's fill-based rules but unnecessary with a weight trigger. Read the labelled share as a lower bound and the model's share as an upper estimate.

virtual_scale.reading: A model trained on a few reference devices estimates every other device's lift weight from signals the compactor already has; compaction cycles and time since the last lift halve the error compared with fill alone. A handful of shared weighbridge tickets per device calibrate it further. Beyond ~5 % reference devices, more reference scales add little.
